bihar_raw_news.title: Jamui school securing 2nd rank in country, matter of pride for Bihar : CM - Awaz The Voice
bihar_raw_news.content: Jamui school securing 2nd rank in country, matter of pride for Bihar: CM Story by PTI | Posted by Ashhar Alam | Date 19-10-2026 Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Patna Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Friday congratulated the students and teachers of Jamui's Simultala Awasiya Vidyalaya after the school recently secured second rank nationally in the C-Fore School Ranking 2026. The school secured the second position nationally under the category of Government Residential Schools in the prestigious C-Fore School Rankings 2026. While Motilal Nehru School of Sports secured the first spot, Oak Grove School stood third. "Jamui's Simultala Awasiya Vidyalaya securing the second rank nationally in the C-Fore School Ranking 2026 is a matter of pride for Bihar's talent and academic excellence," Choudhary wrote in a post on X. bihar_raw_news.title: AI infra boom faces data center financing risks - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: Investments & Deals 1 min Read AI infra boom faces data center financing risks Goldman Sachs highlights growing financing risks in the expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure sector, particularly concerning data centre bonds. Investors should assess individual projects for potential risks before investing, amidst rising demand for computing capacity. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 19, 2026 at 01:10 PM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights Goldman Sachs highlights financing risks in AI infrastructure and data centre bonds. High-yield data centre bonds face pressure as investors assess expansion risks. Investors must evaluate individual projects for construction, repayment, and regulatory risks. Power availability and insurance are critical factors for project viability. Goldman Sachs research indicates increasing concerns about financing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, questioning whether credit markets can sustain the massive investments required for data centres. High-yield bonds issued by data centre companies are facing pressure as investors evaluate the risks of rapid AI infrastructure expansion, the report stated. Amanda Lynam from Goldman Sachs' credit research team emphasised that investors must examine construction risks, loan repayment ability, refinancing requirements, and claims against tenants when assessing data centre projects. She also cited power availability , regulatory approvals , and insurance as crucial factors affecting project viability . The report stressed that financial risks need individual project-level assessment, rather than assuming all AI infrastructure investments carry similar risks. This individual assessment approach is also vital for equity investors as companies across sectors increase their exposure to data centres, potentially taking on higher investment risks . The report mentioned Spanish renewable energy company Solaria 's data centre deal in Uruguay as an example of the link between energy firms and data centre infrastructure. Goldman Sachs analyst Alberto Gandolfi believes the risks associated with the Solaria deal are skewed to the upside, with further announcements possible at its capital markets day in November. national_raw_news.title: PM Modi wishes Indian contingent success as Asian Para Games open in Aichi-Nagoya
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday extended his best wishes to India’s contingent as the Asian Para Games 2026 opened in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, praising the athletes’ determination and sporting spirit. “As the Asian Para Games 2026 begin in Aichi-Nagoya, conveying my best wishes to the Indian contingent,” PM Modi said in a post on X. “India is immensely proud of our phenomenal para-athletes. Their grit, dedication and indomitable spirit inspire 140 crore Indians. May they compete with confidence and give their very best,” he added. Para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma led the Indian delegation as flag-bearers at the opening ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya. The contingent wore deep blue blazers with golden motifs inspired by the Indus Valley Civilisation, incorporating the Priest-King sculpture, Dancing Girl figurine and ancient seals. India’s 281-member delegation comprises 168 athletes, 98 team officials and support personnel, and 15 contingent staff. The athletes—112 men and 56 women—will compete across 11 disciplines during the Games, which conclude on October 24. India enters the competition after its best-ever Asian Para Games performance in Hangzhou, where it won 111 medals – 29 gold, 31 silver and 51 bronze – surpassing its previous best of 72 medals at Jakarta in 2018. Head coach of para-athletics Satyanarayana said India was targeting around 100 medals and hoped to make a strong start. “Para athletics will be a crucial part of our medal campaign. We are expecting to win six medals in athletics tomorrow, including two to three gold medals,” he said ahead of the opening ceremony. He added that Nishad Kumar was in good form and could challenge his personal best and the Games record. “The competition will be tough, with some of the best athletes from across Asia participating, but our athletes are well prepared and focused on performing to their potential, winning medals and making the country proud,” Satyanarayana said. Para-athletics contributed 55 medals, including 18 gold, to India’s tally in 2023 and is again expected to play a leading role. Two-time Paralympic champion Sumit Antil will seek to defend his men’s javelin F64 title. The athletics squad also includes Paralympic champions Dharambir Nain, Praveen Kumar and Navdeep Singh, alongside Paralympic medallists Preethi Pal, Deepthi Jeevanji, Nishad Kumar, Sachin Sarjerao Khilari and Hokato Hotozhe Sema. Two-time Paralympic champion Avani Lekhara leads India’s para-shooting challenge and will defend her Asian Para Games women’s 10-metre air rifle title. In para-archery, 19-year-old Sheetal Devi returns to defend her women’s compound title after a multiple-medal campaign in 2023. Paralympic champions Nitesh Kumar and Pramod Bhagat spearhead the para-badminton team, which also features Paralympic silver medallists Suhas Yathiraj and Thulasimathi Murugesan, and bronze medallist Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan. Bhagat has won six Asian Para Games medals between 2014 and 2023, including two gold and four bronze. Fellow flag-bearer Simran won a women’s 200-metre bronze at the 2024 Paralympics and two silver medals at the previous Asian Para Games. India’s medal tally has risen from 14 at Guangzhou in 2010 to 33 at Incheon in 2014, 72 at Jakarta in 2018 and 111 at Hangzhou in 2023. This edition’s competitions will be held across 19 venues, with Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium serving as the main arena. (With agency inputs)

national_raw_news.title: Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam ...
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 in Mysuru, Karnataka Nine Days Mela Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans 12 States, Union Territories Participating in the Mela Secretary Reiterates Government’s Commitment To Ensure Strong Market Access, Encourage Entrepreneurship And Advance Economic Empowerment Of Disadvantaged Communities Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi The Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant visited the ongoing Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, at Mysuru in Karnataka this evening. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry through joint partnership of three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries. During the visit to Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, the Secretary inspected stalls and talked to the Stall Managers and visitors. The Union Secretary is on a two days official visit to Mysuru to take comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the Administration. He is also undertaking Site Visits in Mysuru. Shri Pant said through such initiatives, the Ministry continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities. The Shilp Samagam Mela continues until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans. A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is underway since October 11 and provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience. The Official informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition. He said the stalls feature with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience. The Official further said the Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills, he added.
